memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses built an altar and called it The LORD is my Banner. He said, 'Because
hands were lifted up against the throne of the LORD, the LORD will be at war
against the Amalekites from generation to generation.'" - Ex 17:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses' response to victory is to build an altar. Not a monument to Joshua, not a
victory column. An altar, which is a place of worship.

And he gives it a name: The LORD is my Banner.

A banner in the ancient world was the standard an army rallied around. It marked
who you belonged to and where to gather when the fighting scattered you. Moses
is saying: our identity and our rallying point is the LORD Himself.

Notice the personal word again. Not "the LORD is a banner" but "my Banner."
After a long, exhausting day, Moses claims God as his own.

Isaiah later takes up this image and points it forward. He speaks of a coming
one who "will stand as a banner for the peoples" and to whom "the nations will
rally" (Isa 11:10). Paul quotes that very verse and applies it to Christ (Rom
15:12).

So the banner Moses raised in a desert is finally lifted at a cross, where all
nations are called to gather. Jesus said, "And I, when I am lifted up from the
earth, will draw all people to myself" (John 12:32).

Whatever the day has cost you, there is a place to gather. He is the banner.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What do you rally around when life scatters you?
2. Is your first response to relief worship or simply relief?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are my banner. When I am scattered and worn out, let me gather back to
You. Amen.
